s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic respiratory symptoms with pleural effusion and granular shadows on imaging
salient_findings: Diffuse granular shadows on right side
key_facts: 70-year-old man
History of tuberculous pleurisy seven years before admission
Cough
Bilateral sinusitis on otolaryngology examination
Chest X-ray shows tumor in the center
Chest X-ray shows pleural effusion on left side
Chest X-ray shows diffuse granular shadows on right side
Chest CT shows bronchial wall thickening
Chest CT shows numerous granular shadows
Biopsy shows lymphocyte infiltration
Biopsy shows no fibrosis
Respiratory function test shows decreased forced expiratory volume in 1s
Blood sampling shows high cold agglutinin reaction

differentials: Systemic lupus erythematosus-associated interstitial lung disease
per_call: Systemic lupus erythematosus-associated interstitial lung disease

shortlist.label: Lymphangitic carcinomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chest X-ray shows tumor in the center and pleural effusion, consistent with metastatic disease

shortlist.label: Tuberculous pleurisy
shortlist.why_kept: History of tuberculous pleurisy and current pleural effusion, suggesting possible reactivation

shortlist.label: Pulmonary lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lymphocyte infiltration on biopsy and history of cough, raising concern for lymphoproliferative disorder

shortlist.label: Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Chest X-ray shows diffuse granular shadows and biopsy shows lymphocyte infiltration, consistent with COP

shortlist.label: Churg-Strauss syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral sinusitis, asthma-like symptoms, and eosinophilia suggested by high cold agglutinin reaction, raising concern for CSS

raw.rationale: The presence of a tumor in the center of the chest X-ray, pleural effusion, and diffuse granular shadows, along with bronchial wall thickening and numerous granular shadows on CT, are highly suggestive of lymphangitic carcinomatosis, which is characterized by the spread of cancer to the lymphatic vessels of the lungs.

rejected.label: Tuberculous pleurisy
rejected.why: Although the patient has a history of tuberculous pleurisy, the current findings of a tumor and diffuse granular shadows are not typical of tuberculous pleurisy

rejected.label: Pulmonary lymphoma
rejected.why: While lymphoma could explain some of the findings, the presence of a tumor in the center of the chest X-ray and the pattern of granular shadows are more suggestive of lymphangitic carcinomatosis

rejected.label: Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with more focal consolidation and does not typically cause the widespread granular shadows seen in this patient

rejected.label: Churg-Strauss syndrome
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by asthma, eosinophilia, and vasculitis, which are not mentioned in the case report
